post.title: He Was Told He Would Serve — He Never Did | Genesis 27:40
post.description:
Isaac decreed that Esau would serve his brother. Esau never served him a single day of his life.

He knew he had an option — to serve, or not to serve — and he took responsibility for his own life.

"The power may not necessarily be in what was said to you, but in how you have treated what was said to you." — Pst Emmanuel Omini

If you allow the wrong mindset, you'll begin to live a life of defeat. But you can choose to live against the narrative and walk in victory.

What word are you refusing to bow to this season? Tell us in the comments.

slides.title:
He Was Told
He Would *Serve*.
He Never Did.
slides.sub: There is a prophecy in your Bible that simply… never happened. And the reason why will change how you carry every word ever spoken over you.

slides.verse: By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother; and it shall come to pass, when you become restless, that you shall break his yoke from your neck.

slides.lead: Isaac told Esau that he shall *serve* his brother.
slides.body:
Guess what?

Esau never served Jacob in his lifetime.

Esau *refused* to play to that decree.

He chose his reality.

slides.lead: At that moment, he knew he had an option — to serve, or not to serve.
slides.body: He took *responsibility* for his own life.

slides.quote: The power may not necessarily be in what was said to you, but in *how you have treated* what was said to you.

slides.lead: If you allow the wrong mindset, you'll begin to live a life of defeat.
slides.body: But you can choose to live *against the narrative* — and walk in victory.
